input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The § 12.1 grant is expressly "revocable" with no stated cause standard, i.e. revocable at IBM's discretion, and it runs to "Customer" only — no Affiliates or contractors acting on our behalf, with no notice mechanism to add them. § 14.17 confirms only expressly specified licences are granted, closing off any implied extension. That combination is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice). Transferability is separately satisfied by § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so our redline only removes revocation at will (limiting it to our uncured material breach) and extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors, with a cross-reference to the permitted successor transfer.

proposal.summary: Extend the Base Components licence to Customer Affiliates and contractors, and remove revocability at will
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and limited revocation to our uncured material breach, since our playbook does not accept a licence that is revocable at IBM's discretion or that excludes the group entities and suppliers who actually use the Services. If helpful, we can instead cover Affiliates on written notice to IBM.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license, revocable only for Customer's uncured material breach and transferable to any successor permitted under Section 14.10, to use the Base Components
